seoTitle: How to Get Stock Data in Google Sheets with GOOGLEFINANCE
metaDescription: Use the GOOGLEFINANCE function in Google Sheets to pull live stock prices, historical trends, and metrics like P/E ratio automatically.
intro: Tracking a stock portfolio manually is slow and quickly gets out of date, but Google Sheets has a built-in function that pulls live market data for you. This guide covers the GOOGLEFINANCE formula syntax, from basic real-time prices to historical data and advanced metrics, so you can build an automated tracking spreadsheet.

steps.heading: Learn the basic formula syntax
steps.body: Write a GOOGLEFINANCE formula referencing any stock ticker to start pulling data.

steps.heading: Pull real-time stock prices
steps.body: Use the formula to fetch current price and day-over-day change for a given stock.

steps.heading: Use the correct exchange prefix
steps.body: Add the appropriate market prefix to your ticker to avoid discrepancies between similarly named stocks on different exchanges.

steps.heading: Fetch historical price data
steps.body: Adjust the formula with a start date and interval to pull daily or weekly historical prices.

steps.heading: Extract advanced metrics
steps.body: Pull additional attributes like P/E ratio, market cap, and 52-week highs using the same function.

steps.heading: Build a multi-stock watchlist
steps.body: Combine multiple GOOGLEFINANCE formulas into a dynamic table to track several stocks or currency exchange rates at once.

faq.question: Why is my GOOGLEFINANCE formula pulling the wrong stock?
faq.answer: This usually happens when the exchange prefix is missing or incorrect, causing the formula to match a similarly named ticker on a different exchange.

faq.question: Can I get historical stock prices, not just live data?
faq.answer: Yes, by adding a start date and interval parameter to the formula, you can pull historical daily or weekly price data.

faq.question: Does GOOGLEFINANCE update in real time?
faq.answer: The function is designed to provide near real-time data, though there can be occasional lags depending on the query and market.

faq.question: Can I track currency exchange rates the same way?
faq.answer: Yes, GOOGLEFINANCE also supports pulling currency exchange rate data alongside stock information.
